evidence.snippet: Regulator summary: about 5.2 million customers were moved to the new platform in April 2018.
Regulator summary: the new platform provider relied on 85 third parties of its own that the bank had not assessed, so Customer service recovery could not count on the new platform alone.

Regulator findings mapped to this twin: Customer service recovery depends on the Old platform fallback copy. Once customers move there is no way back, and the new provider's own recovery rests on sub-suppliers nobody assessed.
Regulator summary: the provider had not run a UK bank platform of this kind before.
Regulator summary: 225,492 complaints and about GBP 32.7M redress to customers.
Regulator summary: fines of GBP 29.75M (FCA) and GBP 18.9M (PRA) in December 2022 for operational resilience failings.
Press summary: the owner expected about GBP 160M a year of pre-tax savings by the third full year; the previous owner contributed GBP 450M.
Annual report summary: GBP 330.2M of post-migration charges in 2018; about GBP 153M estimated recovery from the provider was accrued, not yet paid.
Modeled: digital, telephone and branch channels run on the new platform; payments and fraud monitoring depend on the customer ledger.
Modeled: the exit terms with the old host do not say whether a usable copy of the service is kept after exit.
Modeled: channel recovery steps assume a restore point; no rollback rehearsal is recorded.
